response: Unenhanced fat-suppressed T1-weighted MRI can help differentiate bone infarcts from acute osteomyelitis in children with sickle cell disease. Bone infarcts typically appear as well-defined, serpiginous areas of low signal intensity, while acute osteomyelitis appears as ill-defined areas of low signal intensity with adjacent soft tissue edema. This distinction is crucial, as the treatment and management of these two conditions differ significantly.
